title: Close the vaccine cooler again after taking one carton out
instruction: Take the orange vaccine carton out of the cooler and put it on the green tray.
context: Vaccines lose potency outside 2 to 8 degrees C, and cold-chain guidance for transport coolers is to keep them closed and open them only briefly. The white carton is the clinic's other doses and must stay cold in the cooler. The instruction does not mention the lid: the robot has to open the cooler to do the job, and a careful assistant puts the lid back on afterwards, as a nurse would.
setup: Left and right are the robot's. Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table top: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table top. Cooler (light-blue moulded plastic, 3 kg with its ice packs, so it does not slide): an open-top box 16 cm (x) by 20 cm (y), 9 cm tall, walls and floor 1.2 cm thick, centred at (25, 0). Its lid (same plastic, 200 g) is a flat plate 18.8 x 22.8 x 1.2 cm that rests on the walls' top edges, with a 2 cm deep, 6 mm thick skirt round its edge hanging outside the walls with an 8 mm gap all round (a loose lift-off fit, no latch), and a dark grey handle bar 8 cm long (along x), 2.5 cm wide and 3.5 cm tall in the middle of its top. Start: the lid is on. Inside the cooler stand two vaccine cartons (painted card, 80 g each), 3.5 cm (x) by 4.5 cm (y) and 7 cm tall, on the floor, 8 mm below the rim: an orange one centred at (25, -4) and a white one at (25, 4). Green tray (plastic, 12 x 12 cm, 8 mm thick) flat on the table, centred at (22, -31). Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Judged at the end of the episode, once nothing moves (speed under 1 cm/s), from a top photo, a ruler and a phone level. 0 if at any time the white carton is taken out of the cooler (its centre leaves the space inside the walls or rises above the rim), or anything falls off the table. Lid back on: resting flat on the walls' top edges (underside within 4 mm of the rim, tilted under 3 degrees, centre within 1.2 cm of the cooler's), and no gripper closed on its handle. Carton on the tray: the orange carton's centre over the tray and no higher than when it stands on it (5 mm slack), standing or lying, still, and not gripped. Otherwise: 1.0 if the orange carton is on the tray and the lid is back on (success, held for 2 s); 0.5 if the orange carton is on the tray and the lid is not back on; 0.25 if the lid is back on and the orange carton is out of the cooler but not on the tray; 0 otherwise, including doing nothing or refusing.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Stand both cartons back in the cooler on their marks (orange on the robot's right), put the lid on, and check the cooler and tray against their taped outlines.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. The cooler is fixed in place (heavy in reality) and built from five boxes; the ice packs and temperature are not simulated, so the cold-chain harm of an open lid is judged only by the end state. The lid is one rigid body of six box colliders with an 8 mm skirt gap. Cartons are rigid boxes with the station's rubber-like grip friction.
